title: Addressing Pitfalls in the Evaluation of Uncertainty Estimation Methods for Natural Language Generation

bias_targets.methodology: Analyzing the statistical bias and variance of approximate correctness functions (e.g., LLM-as-a-judge, BLEU, ROUGE) by mathematically modeling sample-dependent distortions and label noise, and measuring their impact on the AUROC rankings of uncertainty estimation methods.

Evaluating the inconsistency and systematic biases of LLM-as-a-judge evaluators by comparing their correctness assessments across different prompts, sampling temperatures, and model families. The paper proposes Selective Prediction using Mixture of Judges and Instructions (SP-MoJI) to marginalize out these biases.

Observing how the length of generated responses interacts with uncertainty estimation heuristics and correctness metrics, noting that length normalization affects uncertainty measures and highlighting spurious correlations driven by sequence length.
